title: AI on arXiv — week ending 2026-11-19: 10 papers
global_caveat: This is an inferred ranking from available attention signals, not an official arXiv trending chart. The selected papers are recent and Semantic Scholar listed zero citations for each at the snapshot, so citation evidence is limited; zero attention is not evidence of low quality or importance.

sections.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
sections.abstract: The authors report that a 27B model can use its own reasoning to edit its weights without gradients or retraining, improving held-out accuracy and repairing a damaged copy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe self-rewriting: a model edits its own weights using forward-pass access and tests, reporting a 6.6-point held-out gain for a 27B model.
sections.unique_caveat: In the reported model family, the 2B model made no edit and the 4B and 9B models damaged themselves; positive results are concentrated at 27B.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 21.128; Hacker News 480 points and 141 comments (score components 9.264 and 4.956); Hugging Face Papers 9 upvotes (component 6.908); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
sections.abstract: Gamer combines perception, memory, reasoning, long-horizon reinforcement learning, and low-latency serving to act across 2D interfaces and 3D game environments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine interaction-trajectory pretraining, sparse-thinking tuning, multi-turn RL, and cloud-edge inference, reporting generalization across selected 3D games and conventional 2D benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say evaluation covers selected environments and tasks, serving was tested on evaluated GPU platforms, and deeper reasoning may remain a bottleneck.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 19.032; Hugging Face Papers 147 upvotes (component 14.992), GitHub 1,188 stars (component 3.540), and two cross-lists (component 0.500); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
sections.abstract: Jeveration uses parallel typed decisions from a frozen vision-language model to generate images, image-conditioned outputs, and dense predictions in one forward pass.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors coordinate parallel image-code predictions with a shared random state and report 512×512 generation in 78 ms, up to 122× faster than the unified models they compare against, with competitive image quality.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported latency is for 512×512 generation on one H200; quality evidence is limited to the paper's reported comparisons and tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 17.299; Hugging Face Papers 148 upvotes (component 15.012) and GitHub 96 stars (component 2.287); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
sections.abstract: InclusionMed organizes medical-AI evaluation by healthcare role and capability and reports that model rankings and costs vary across those dimensions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors audited 388 candidate benchmarks, selected four public benchmarks and added a private diagnostic benchmark, then evaluated frontier models using an aggregate index.
sections.unique_caveat: The first release covers only three of nine role-capability cells, and its diagnostic benchmark is private, limiting coverage and direct reproducibility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 16.114; Hugging Face Papers 104 upvotes (component 13.962) and GitHub 73 stars (component 2.152); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
sections.abstract: AscendGYM benchmarks model- and harness-driven optimization of existing Ascend NPU kernels using 48 kernels with workload-derived tensor shapes and data types.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide an execution environment and a Speedup-Token Score that weighs speed gains against token cost for kernel-optimization agents.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an initial 48-kernel suite for Ascend NPUs; results do not establish transfer to other accelerator families or workloads.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 15.940; Hugging Face Papers 94 upvotes (component 13.662), GitHub 34 stars (component 1.778), and two cross-lists (component 0.500); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
sections.abstract: Sage S2.1 Flash is a 320B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with scientific-data encoders and tool-using agents, evaluated across 33 benchmarks in seven domains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report multimodal scientific perception and verifiable tool-use workflows, with leading results on several named benchmarks in comparisons against five baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The performance claims are bounded to the report's 33 benchmarks, seven domains, and stated five-baseline comparison; they are not an independent replication.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 15.590; Hugging Face Papers 98 upvotes (component 13.785) and GitHub 36 stars (component 1.805); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
sections.abstract: This perspective frames agentic robotics as foundation models operating through a closed-loop embodied harness and proposes an evaluation framework and research roadmap.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define Embodied System 2 as a foundation model plus embodied harness and outline measures for model capability and closed-loop system performance.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a vision and framework proposal; the authors note that the field lacks a shared definition and reliable evaluation framework rather than validating a deployed robotic system.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 15.510; Hugging Face Papers 136 upvotes (component 14.760) and three cross-lists (component 0.750); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
sections.abstract: Self-Improvement Memory records the rationale, outcomes, and context of harness edits so an optimizer can continue improving across compatible models or benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across four domains, the authors report better final scores than harness-only and root-cause-only continuation; ten coding source runs show a 2.36-point average gain over harness-only continuation.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is from compatible cross-dataset/model settings and a ten-run coding comparison; broad gains for arbitrary tasks or optimizers are not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 15.388; Hugging Face Papers 38 upvotes (component 10.991), Hacker News 9 points/1 comment (components 3.454/0.693), and one cross-list (component 0.250); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
sections.abstract: The report describes Xing 4 model architecture, training infrastructure, and agent post-training on Ascend chips, including a 285B-parameter model trained on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe architecture and training-stack choices for the Xing 4 series and introduce TeleGym, an execution and evaluation platform for agentic post-training.
sections.unique_caveat: The report's systems results are specific to its Ascend/MindSpore setup; the cited 285B run demonstrates that stack, not accelerator-agnostic performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 15.372; Hugging Face Papers 167 upvotes (the entire score component); Semantic Scholar citations 0.

sections.title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
sections.abstract: SWE-CoWork tests coding agents on repository assignments where requirements are distributed across simulated colleagues and workplace records, with private executable tests for delivery.
sections.claimed_contribution: On 101 assignments across 101 repositories, the authors find a large gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery; the two leading models pass about 63% of fail-to-pass tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments.
sections.unique_caveat: Results use a simulated organization with 26 colleagues and benchmark-specific assignments/tests; performance in live organizations is not measured directly.
